newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INTERVIEW-Austrim not planning to hike bid.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Austrim not planning to hike bid.

text.p: Austrim Ltd Managing Director Alan Jackson said on Monday the takeover bid by his investment group for car components manufacturer Hawker Richardson Ltd was fully priced and he was not considering increasing it.
Jackson told Reuters in an interview the acquisition would be earnings per share positive.

Earlier Hawker Richardson said the A$1.60 a share offer price, which values the company at A$58.31 million, was "possibly a bit low" and that brokers and investors thought a higher price might be bid by either Austrim or a rival.
"I guess the punters are there at the moment hoping something else might happen, but we've decided not to fiddle and we've come with a full price, right up front," Jackson said.
"There'd be no consideration of that at this time," he said when asked if the price would be raised.
Jackson said Austrim had stated for a year that it wanted to be involved in the industrial manufacturing sector and that it was looking at the automotive componenet sector in particular.
He said the sector had underperfomed in the past and that recent shares prices refected that disappointment.
But Austrim had been waiting for the government's decision to freeze car import tariffs at 10 percent from 2000 to January 2005 and was now satisfied with the sector's outlook, he said.
"The government's cleared the air on that completely and I think that it's a good opportunity and it fits perfectly in terms of our industrial manufacturing strategy," he said.
Jackson said Austrim was not currently looking at acquiring other automotive component makers, but that he would not rule out looking at others in the future.
He said Hawker Richardson's turnover represented about 130 percent of the takeover bid price and that the price to earnings ratio bid was at the top end of prices offered in the sector.
The A$1.60 per share bid represented 11.5 times actual earnings per share (EPS) in the year to June 30, 1996, 10.3 times consensus forecast EPS in calendar 1997 and 8.9 times forecast EPS in 1998.

The latest acquisition, which follows the A$41 million acquisition of a vehicle hire and workshop business from the South Australian Commissioner of Highways in March and the A$53 million purchase of Calum textiles in February, would be the last in the currrent financial year to June 30, Jackson said.
Austrim would now focus on getting its gearing levels down from its current level of about 125 percent of debt to shareholders funds.

"My record is one of trying to always have gearing at a relatively low level -- 30 to 40 percent -- and to bring us back to that we will need to consider at some point in the future, a general rights issue," Jackson said.
Earlier, Austrim announced a 14 million share placement to institutional investors at A$3.00 a share to raise A$42 million to partly pay for the Hawker acquisition.
It also announced it was considering a pro-rata rights issue to reduce debt and that a final decision would be taken in the third quarter of calendar 1997.
Jackson said he could not say how much the rights issue would be for, but that the aim was to start reducing gearing towards 40 percent from the current 125 percent.
Austrim's shares were up four cents at A$3.09 at 3.15 p.m. (0515 GMT).
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
